newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Clashes on Somali-Ethiopian border leave 13 dead.
newsitem.headline: Clashes on Somali-Ethiopian border leave 13 dead.

text.p: Ethiopian forces fired artillery across the border into a Somali town on Monday night after shells fired at each other by rival Somali factions landed on the Ethiopian side, residents said on Tuesday.
Somali militiamen of the Moslem fundamentalist al-Ittihad al-Islam group said they had killed five Ethiopian soldiers and lost eight of their own men in the fight for Dolow town.

But residents, quoted by aid officials, said the fighting was between al-Ittihad and the rival Somali National Front (SNF) movement and they could not confirm that Ethiopian troops had been involved in the ground fighting.
Residents said shells fired by at least one of the factions slammed into Ethiopian territory and Ethiopia responded by shelling the Somali side of Dolow which straddles the border.
The town was the scene of heavy fighting on Monday between al-Ittihad and the SNF, aid officials quoted residents there as saying.

"It was very heavy. It seems al-Ittihad came in and attacked the SNF in Dolow and Dr Ali Nuur, the deputy chairman of the SNF, was killed along with two other SNF," a Western aid official told Reuters.
"The bridge linking Dolow-Somalia to Dolow-Ethiopia was destroyed on Monday night and shells went from Dolow-Somalia to Dolow-Ethiopia on the other side of the bridge," the aid official added.
"The Ethiopian army retaliated and shelled the hell out of Dolow-Somalia," said the official.

Ahmed Bile, secretary of al-Ittihad, told reporters in Mogadishu his group had seized Dolow town in western Somalia on Monday night. He said five Ethiopian soldiers and eight Ittihad militiamen were killed in the fighting and added part of Dolow was bombarded by Ethiopian artillery.
There was no comment from the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa on the reports of Ethiopian involvement.

Ethiopian troops backed by helicopter gunships and artillery mounted a two-day incursion into the Gedo district of western Somalia last month in support of the SNF against al-Ittihad, which was blamed by Addis Ababa for recent bombings in Ethiopia.
Ethiopia said its raid was directed against fundamentalist bases and training camps and more than 200 people were killed.

In 1977, Somali government forces invaded Ethiopia and within three months had overrun the Ogaden border region, to the north of Dolow. But Ethiopia recaptured the Ogaden in 1978 in a Soviet and Cuban-led counterattack.

In an unrelated development, seven refugees were killed and five wounded when three mortars hit Shabelle camp on Monday night in the southern part of the Somali capital Mogadishu, camp elders said on Tuesday. It was unclear who fired the mortars.
